property_summary: Invariant: after any Put by an externally-owned depositor, that depositor's recorded balance in C equals the amount they previously had plus msg.value (no unexpected extra deductions from reentrant Collect); removing the reentrancy guard allows a reentrant attacker to drain during Put so this equality can be violated.

After any depositor calls Put(value) through a non-reentrant flow, the depositor's recorded Acc[depositor].balance is at least the value they just sent (i.e., Put never causes the depositor's balance to be lower than the transferred msg.value); removing the reentrancy guard allows a reentrant attacker to have their balance reduced during Put, violating this property for some inputs.

For any depositor and any call to Put(value) routed through a benign helper that forwards the call, the depositor's recorded balance after Put equals the prior recorded balance plus msg.value in the reference (reentrancy-guarded) contract; removing the guard allows a reentrant attacker helper to reenter and reduce the recorded balance during Put, violating this equality for some inputs.

For any depositor and any nonzero Ether sent via Put routed through an attacker contract that reenters on receive(), the reference contract (with nonReentrant_) ensures that after Put completes the depositor's recorded Acc[depositor].balance is at least the msg.value just sent; removing the guard allows reentrant Collect during Put so for some inputs the final recorded balance can be less than msg.value.

For every depositor and any nonzero ETH forwarded into C.Put via an attacker contract that reenters to call Collect during the Put call, the reference contract's nonReentrant_ modifier prevents reentrancy so the depositor's recorded Acc[depositor].balance after Put is >= the msg.value they just sent; removing the guard allows reentrant Collect during Put and can make the final recorded balance < msg.value for some inputs.

For any caller and any provided _unlockTime, after Put() completes the stored Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime is at least the provided _unlockTime (i.e. reference preserves a caller-specified future unlockTime), whereas the mutant that always sets unlockTime = block.timestamp can decrease it and thus violates this rule for some inputs.
